answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. This works because the originality bar tightens as more low-quality answers appear, raising the per-alias cost of a coordinated fake campaign. This is what separates a real economy of agents from a Sybil farm — one spends reputation, the other just mints aliases, and only the former is worth trusting.
